extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, authors, and reviewers interested in peer review workflows (particularly Cell Press's Community Review)
extracted.subtask_description: A publisher-run parallel/Community Review workflow where a single review process assesses fit across multiple in-house journals, producing a decision letter that gives authors options and a tailored revision plan. The page describes how the system works, roles, constraints, and success metrics for a Cell Press pilot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal fit / suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors submit and indicate which Cell Press journals they are interested in; the Community Editor consults with expert editors at the relevant individual journals and reviewers are asked for their opinion on suitability for those journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system assesses 'fit' in parallel rather than sequentially. If a mismatch exists between authors' journal choices and where editors see the best fit, this feedback is discussed with authors before proceeding to review. Final judgments about whether a paper is a good fit come primarily from the dedicated editors of the individual journals, who retain the right to refuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured reviewer feedback (strengths and limitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are shown the list of journals authors have expressed interest in and complete a structured reviewer form asking for specific comments, primarily aimed at understanding the strengths and limitations of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structured, targeted reviewer comments are intended to give authors clear feedback and enable editors to make informed assessments of fit. Reviewers are also asked for their opinion on suitability for particular journals, which feeds into the decision process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Editor coordination and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: A dedicated Community Editor does an initial review, consults with scientific editors at individual journals, coordinates reviewer invitations across the journals involved, formulates a decision letter outlining options, and discusses revision plans with authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community Editors are trained Cell Press editors who read broadly and tap into the expertise of individual journal Scientific Editors and external reviewers. They coordinate cross-consultation among editors and reviewers, and may discuss with authors if authors' journal choices appear mismatched. Their role is central to guiding papers through the single review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single review process; no new journal-level review rounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The review process is conducted in the Community Review system in consultation with individual journal editors; by the time a paper transfers to a specific journal, the intention is that the paper should already be through the final steps needed before acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The idea is to avoid repeating full rounds of peer review at each journal. However, the system allows for nuance: if revisions do not pan out as anticipated, plans may change and additional review steps could arise as a contingency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author choice among publication options and tailored revision plans
rubrics_metrics.description: After review, the Community Editor consults with journal representatives to formulate a decision letter that outlines options in terms of the type of revisions (if any) different journals would be looking for; the author then discusses and selects a plan and resubmits accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can choose how to proceed based on the feedback and their particular situation (e.g., aiming for a higher-tier journal might require more extensive revisions). The Community Editor helps authors think about appropriate audience and fit. A noted anti-pattern is that authors in need of speed may choose journals that require no revisions, which could be suboptimal for scientific development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain journal-specific editorial and publishing criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial and publishing criteria for individual journals are not changed by Community Review; if editors of a given journal don't think a submitted paper is a good fit, they will not proceed with publishing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community Review coordinates assessment but does not override journal standards. Decisions about fit and acceptance rest with journal-dedicated editors, preserving each journal's thresholds and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-house journal limitation and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can currently choose any number of Cell Press life science journals, but the system is limited to Cell Press journals because it relies on close and efficient cooperation among in-house professional editors and confidentiality/access to internal systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In principle external academic editors or external journals could be included, but that would require adjustments for confidentiality, access to reviewer/journal databases, and cooperation logistics. The current setup intentionally avoids external partners while the pilot is tested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot success metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The pilot will be evaluated on whether it helps more authors get published efficiently and constructively, with specific aims of increasing ultimate acceptance decisions, reducing time to publication, and decreasing total reviewer effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cell Press will gather ongoing feedback from participating authors and reviewers to refine the system. Potential additional options (e.g., transparent peer review, portable peer review) could be layered on later. Metrics to monitor include acceptance rate after Community Review, time from submission to publication, number of reviews per paper, and participant satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: No simultaneous publication in multiple journals
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Community Editor and editors find an article suitable for more than one journal, the authors will be given a choice of which journal to proceed with; papers will not be published in two journals at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although fit for multiple journals may be recognized, the system is designed to result in a single journal of publication. Authors may select which audience and revision focus to pursue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-consultation, flexibility, and contingency for revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The process includes cross-consultation among reviewers, discussion with editors, and the possibility of changing the planned route if revisions don't pan out as anticipated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The workflow is deliberately flexible to accommodate many variations that arise in publishing. Editors and Community Editors may adjust plans midstream and re-evaluate fit or next steps if revision outcomes differ from expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risks and anti-patterns (business incentives, internal ranking, and capture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commentary raises concerns that publisher-run cascading/community systems can serve business strategies (keeping manuscripts 'in-house'), require implicit internal ranking of journals, and may incentivize authors to choose routes that favor publisher interests or rapid, minimal-revision publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are cautionary considerations to monitor: implement transparency around ranking/decisioning where feasible, protect author choice, ensure incentives do not undermine scientific quality, and be mindful of brand/market effects (publisher-first branding). The Community Review design and feedback loops should address and mitigate these risks.
